header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH AT KARACHI
[Nasi Ahmed Shah V. Shazia Erum and others]
DATE ORDER WITH SIGNATURE OF JUDGE(S).
1. For orders on CMA No.8254/2026 (If granted).
2. For orders on office objection No.15 at flag “A”.
Petitioner Nasi Ahmed Shah present in person.
body: Abdul Hamid Bhurgri, J.- The petitioner has invoked the constitutional jurisdiction of this Court under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, challenging the judgment dated 28.09.2026, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Karachi Central, in Family Appeal No.104/2025, whereby his appeal against the order of the learned Family Court/Executing Court, arising out of Family Suit No.2783/2022, was dismissed as not maintainable under Section 14 of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act, 1964.

2. The petitioner, appearing in person, contends that his daughter, aged about 25 years, is gainfully employed as an Electrical Engineer with K-Electric and is financially independent; therefore, he is no longer liable to pay her maintenance. He further submits that he has remained unemployed since 2024 and is suffering from health issues. He also disputes the continuation of maintenance for his son after attaining majority, the calculation of outstanding maintenance and the adjustment of amounts already deposited.

3. Heard the petitioner and perused the available record. The controversy essentially relates to the execution of a subsisting maintenance decree. It is a settled principle of law that an Executing Court can neither go behind the decree nor travel beyond its terms. It is bound to execute the decree as it stands and cannot alter, modify or question its correctness, except to the extent permissible under law. The petitioner’s plea regarding his daughter’s alleged financial independence and his own inability to pay cannot, by itself, extinguish the liability arising under a subsisting decree. Such contentions, insofar as they seek modification or cessation of the decretal liability, must be agitated before the competent forum through an appropriate legal remedy and cannot be entertained as objections to its execution.

4. The learned Appellate Court, while dismissing the appeal as not maintainable under Section 14 of the Act, has nevertheless addressed the petitioner’s grievances concerning verification of the son’s date of attaining majority, adjustment of amounts already deposited and consideration of his application under Section 13(5) of the Act for payment of the decretal amount by installments. These matters have appropriately been left for determination by the Executing Court in accordance with law. The reference to Paragraph 370 of Mulla’s Principles of Mahomedan Law does not furnish any independent ground for interference with the impugned judgment, particularly when the subsisting decree remains binding and enforceable unless varied or set aside by a competent forum.

5. It is equally well settled that constitutional jurisdiction under Article 199 of the Constitution cannot be invoked as a substitute for an appeal or other statutory remedy, nor can it be exercised merely to reopen concluded adjudications. Interference is warranted where an order suffers from a jurisdictional defect, patent illegality, material irregularity affecting the exercise of jurisdiction or violation of law. No such infirmity has been demonstrated in the present case. Entertaining the petition on the grounds urged would effectively permit the petitioner to circumvent the finality of the maintenance decree and obstruct its lawful execution, which is impermissible.

6. For the foregoing reasons, the petition is misconceived, devoid of merit and does not disclose any ground warranting interference under Article 199 of the Constitution. It is accordingly dismissed in limine, along with all pending applications. The Executing Court shall proceed in accordance with law, give effect to the directions contained in the impugned judgment and decide the petitioner’s pending application under Section 13(5) of the Act, if not already decided, through a reasoned order. Nothing observed herein shall prejudice any remedy otherwise available to the petitioner before the competent forum in accordance with law.
